name: jQuery
tagline: A lightweight library for DOM, events and AJAX.
timeTravelLog: Released in 2006 by John Resig, jQuery solved the greatest crisis of the web era — inconsistent browser APIs. It unified DOM manipulation, events, and AJAX across browsers with a single syntax.
overview: jQuery is a fast, small, and feature-rich JavaScript library that simplifies HTML document traversal, event handling, animation, and AJAX with an easy-to-use API that works across a multitude of browsers.

syllabus.title: Module 1: The $ Selector Engine
syllabus.desc: Using jQuery's powerful selector syntax to target any DOM element.
syllabus.content: jQuery's core is the $() function — it accepts any CSS selector string and returns a jQuery object wrapping all matched elements. You can chain methods on the result. $(document).ready() ensures your code runs only after the entire DOM is parsed and available.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Modern shorthand: $(function() { ... }) is identical to $(document).ready() — it automatically defers execution until the DOM is fully parsed and ready!

syllabus.title: Module 2: DOM Manipulation (Read & Write Content)
syllabus.desc: Changing element text, HTML, attributes, and CSS properties on the fly.
syllabus.content: jQuery methods are getter/setter combos — called with no argument they read the current value; called with an argument they set it across all matched elements. .text() gets/sets text content. .html() gets/sets innerHTML. .val() gets/sets form input values. .attr() and .prop() handle attributes and properties.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Avoid using .html() with untrusted user data — it's vulnerable to XSS injection! Use .text() for displaying user-provided strings safely without executing embedded HTML tags.

syllabus.title: Module 3: CSS & Class Management
syllabus.desc: Dynamically styling elements by adding, removing, and toggling CSS classes.
syllabus.content: jQuery provides clean methods for CSS class management. .addClass() appends a class. .removeClass() strips a class. .toggleClass() flips a class on/off — perfect for interactive state toggles. .css() reads or sets inline CSS properties directly, accepting single properties or objects for batch updates.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Prefer .addClass() and .removeClass() over .css() for styling — it separates concerns (HTML/CSS/JS) and makes styles maintainable from your stylesheet rather than scattered in JS code!

syllabus.title: Module 4: Event Handling (click, hover, keyup, on())
syllabus.desc: Listening and responding to user interactions across the page.
syllabus.content: .on() is the universal jQuery event binding method — it attaches any event listener to matched elements. Shorthand methods .click(), .hover(), .keyup(), .submit() are convenient aliases. Event delegation via .on(event, selector, handler) efficiently handles events on dynamically created elements.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Always use event delegation ($parent.on(event, childSelector, handler)) for dynamically generated elements — events bound directly to elements that don't exist yet won't fire!

syllabus.title: Module 5: Animations (show, hide, fadeIn, slideToggle)
syllabus.desc: Adding smooth built-in animations to create engaging interactive feedback.
syllabus.content: jQuery ships with common animations for showing and hiding elements. .show()/.hide() toggle display visibility. .fadeIn()/.fadeOut() animate opacity. .slideDown()/.slideUp()/.slideToggle() animate height. All accept duration strings ('slow', 'fast') or millisecond values, and an optional callback function that fires when animation completes.
syllabus.interactiveTip: jQuery animations queue by default — multiple method calls chain one after another. Use .stop(true, true) before starting a new animation to clear the queue and jump to the end state!

syllabus.title: Module 6: AJAX ($.ajax, $.get, $.post)
syllabus.desc: Loading and sending data to servers without page reloads.
syllabus.content: jQuery's AJAX methods simplify XMLHttpRequest API. $.get() fetches data. $.post() sends form data. $.ajax() provides full control with method, headers, data, success, and error callbacks. $.getJSON() parses JSON responses automatically. All return Deferred objects (jQuery's Promise-like API) for chaining .done(), .fail(), and .always() handlers.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Modern projects use the native Fetch API or Axios instead of $.ajax. But in legacy codebases, $.ajax's built-in request queuing, global event hooks, and IE support make it invaluable!

syllabus.title: Module 7: jQuery Plugins & chaining
syllabus.desc: Extending jQuery with third-party plugins and mastering method chaining.
syllabus.content: jQuery's most powerful pattern is method chaining — each method returns the jQuery object, so multiple operations flow in a single readable line. Third-party plugins extend the $.fn namespace to add custom methods. Popular jQuery plugins include Slick (carousels), DataTables (sortable grids), Select2 (enhanced dropdowns), and Fancybox (lightboxes).
syllabus.interactiveTip: Always return this from jQuery plugins — it preserves the jQuery object for further chaining. Without return this, your plugin breaks the chain and becomes a dead end!

quiz.question: What does the $() function in jQuery return?
options: A jQuery object wrapping all matched elements
quiz.explanation: $() returns a jQuery object — a special wrapper around matched DOM elements that provides all jQuery methods for chaining. It can wrap single or multiple elements simultaneously.

quiz.question: Why is event delegation preferred for dynamically added elements?
options: It makes code run faster on all browsers
It attaches the listener to a parent that already exists, so it catches events from future child elements
It is the only way to listen to custom events
It prevents memory leaks by auto-removing listeners
quiz.explanation: Event delegation attaches a listener to a parent element that exists in the DOM. When a child (even dynamically added later) triggers the event, it bubbles up to the parent where the handler catches it.

quiz.question: What does .toggleClass() do in jQuery?
options: Creates a new CSS class and applies it
Adds the class if absent, removes it if present
Reads the current class list of an element
quiz.explanation: .toggleClass() adds the specified class if the element doesn't have it, or removes it if it already does — perfect for binary state toggling like open/closed, active/inactive.

quest.title: Project: Build an Interactive Task Logger
quest.challenge: Build a jQuery-powered task log that adds, highlights, and removes entries dynamically.
instructions: 1. Create a text input and an 'Add Entry' button.
2. On button click, use jQuery to append the input value as a new <li> inside a #task-log <ul>.
3. Use event delegation to attach a 'Remove' button to each entry that removes its parent <li>.
4. Add a 'Highlight All' button that toggles a glowing yellow class on all log entries.
5. Add a 'Clear Log' button with a fadeOut animation before emptying the list.
